title: Nature-derived color families

location.series: Pentagram / Natural History Museum case study
location.extent: Published video poster and complete associated clip

slide_intent: Explain color through relationships to subject matter, because a broad palette needs a reason to feel coherent.
strategic_value: Linking swatches with natural imagery can connect the Museum’s varied colors to the diversity it represents.
demonstration: The animation sequences green/yellow, blue/purple and warm pink/red swatch families alongside nature details, then presents multicolor NHM symbols on dark fields. No numeric color values or usage ratios are shown.
practical_value: Compare palette families with their visual references and test a ring combination against its ground.

content_islands.name: Swatch families
content_islands.spec: Arrange broad vertical color bands and change between warm, cool and green families.

content_islands.name: Natural references
content_islands.spec: Replace sections of the bands with creatures, plants, water and other natural details.

content_islands.name: Symbol examples
content_islands.spec: Show different colored ring combinations on dark central fields.

reference_purposes.Expression: The animation sequences green/yellow, blue/purple and warm pink/red swatch families alongside nature details, then presents multicolor NHM symbols on dark fields. No numeric color values or usage ratios are shown.
reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram states that the broad palette reflects diversity in nature and life and invites audiences from different backgrounds.

ingredient.name: Nature-linked color families
ingredient.role: Connect a broad palette to the Museum’s subject matter.
ingredient.application: Compare warm, cool and green color groups with their adjacent natural references.
ingredient.scope: This film explains relationships rather than production values or numeric use ratios.
